'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often referred to as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It was [[self-released]] in July 2001 to moderate sales and little critical attention. 

In April 2002, [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] reissued ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. It became a [[sleeper hit]] in both countries, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States. The EP was favorably received by music critics; it placed second on ''[[NME]]''<nowiki/>'s list of the best singles of 2002, and 42nd on [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']]'s list of the greatest EPs ever made.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often referred to as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It was [[self-released]] in July 2001 to moderate sales and little critical attention. 

In April 2002, [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] reissued ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. It became a [[sleeper hit]] in both countries, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States. The EP was favorably received by music critics; it placed second on ''[[NME]]''<nowiki/>'s list of the best singles of 2002, and 42nd on [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']]'s list of the greatest EPs ever made.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics, with the British press in particular lauding the record. At [[Metacritic]], which assigns a [[Standard score|normalized]] rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, the EP received an [[Weighted arithmetic mean|average]] score of 73, indicating "generally favorable reviews". Heather Phares of ''[[AllMusic]]'' believed it cemented the band as "the artiest and most challenging" group in the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]], while [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']]'s Rob Kemp said it made Karen O the most exciting rock star of the time. [[Everett True]] became infatuated with the record and, in turn, the band, believing they captured the spirit of rock n' roll. Though Chris Dahlen from [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] mocked the general rock movement, he was satisfied with the EP and said it demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities. [[Rob Sheffield]] of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' took issue with its [[sound quality]] and felt it dampened its potential. [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']]'s Kurt Deschermeier praised the first and third tracks but felt the other songs were unremarkable. In 2002, ''[[NME]]'' ranked ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' second on their list of that year's best singles.{{Cite web |date=October 10, 2016 |title=NME's best albums and tracks of 2002 |url=https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124234412/https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |archive-date=January 24, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |website=[[NME]]}} In the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', [[Sasha Frere-Jones]] rated the EP four stars and stated that they "instantly made their case for good-old-fashioned attitude". This scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''. {{Use mdy dates|date=June 2025}} {{Infobox album | name = Yeah Yeah Yeahs | type = EP | artist = [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]] | cover = Yeah_Yeah_Yeahs_(EP).jpg | alt = | released = July 9, 2001 | recorded = | venue = | studio = | genre = {{hlist|[[Garage rock]]|[[indie rock]]|[[alternative rock]]}} | length = 13:52 | label = [[Self-released]] | producer = {{hlist|Jerry Teel|Yeah Yeah Yeahs}} | prev_title = | prev_year = | next_title = [[Machine (EP)|Machine]] | next_year = 2002 }} '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001. In April 2002, [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] reissued ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. It became a [[sleeper hit]] in both countries, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States. The EP was favorably received by music critics; it placed second on ''[[NME]]'''s list of the best singles of 2002, and 42nd on [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']]'s list of the greatest EPs ever made in 2024. == Background and recording == [[File:Yeah Yeah Yeahs (cropped).jpg|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs in 2002]] In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen Orzolek]]—later becoming known as Karen O—and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001. In April 2002, [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] reissued ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. It became a [[sleeper hit]] in both countries, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States. [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']]'s Rob Kemp said it made Karen O the most exciting rock star of the time, and Antonio Santangelo from ''[[CMJ]]'' similarly agreed that she sounded "hot and sexy".{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795}} [[Everett True]] became infatuated with the record and the band, believing they captured the spirit of rock n' roll. [[Rob Sheffield]] of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' took issue with its [[sound quality]] and felt it dampened its potential. [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']]'s Kurt Deschermeier praised the first and third tracks but felt the other songs were unremarkable. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001. 

In April 2002, [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] reissued ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. It became a [[sleeper hit]] in both countries, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States. The EP was favorably received by music critics; it placed second on ''[[NME]]''<nowiki/>'s list of the best singles of 2002, and 42nd on [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']]'s list of the greatest EPs ever made in 2024.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001. 

In April 2002, [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] reissued ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. It became a [[sleeper hit]] in both countries, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States. The EP was favorably received by music critics; it placed second on ''[[NME]]''<nowiki/>'s list of the best singles of 2002, and 42nd on [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']]'s list of the greatest EPs ever made in 2024.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. {{Short description|2001 EP by Yeah Yeah Yeahs}} {{Use mdy dates|date=June 2025}} {{Infobox album | name = Yeah Yeah Yeahs | type = EP | artist = [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]] | cover = Yeah_Yeah_Yeahs_(EP).jpg | alt = | released = July 9, 2001 | recorded = | venue = | studio = | genre = {{hlist|[[Garage rock]]|[[indie rock]]|[[alternative rock]]}} | length = 13:52 | label = [[Self-released]] | producer = {{hlist|Jerry Teel|Yeah Yeah Yeahs}} | prev_title = | prev_year = | next_title = [[Machine (EP)|Machine]] | next_year = 2002 }} '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made. == Background and recording == In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen Orzolek]]—later becoming known as Karen O—and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard. Later that year, they changed their name to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted to a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by their observations of the contemporary Ohio music scene.{{Cite web Although it is self-titled, the EP is sometimes incorrectly referred to as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover. == Music and lyrics == {{Listen | filename = YYYs Bang Sample.ogg | title = "Bang" | description = Sample from "Bang", the EP's opening track }} ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' is a [[garage rock]],{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Betty |date=April 26, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2009/apr/27/yeah-yeahs-pop-review |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}} [[indie rock]], and [[alternative rock]] EP.{{Cite web |date= |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, by Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://yeahyeahyeahs.bandcamp.com/album/yeah-yeah-yeahs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[Bandcamp]] |language=en}} It consists of five tracks and runs for 13 minutes and 52 seconds. The opening track, "Bang", is about Karen O's sexual dissatisfaction with an ex-boyfriend,{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=August 2002 |title=An ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. Themes of sex and [[masturbation]] are further developed in "Mystery Girl", co-written by the band and Jack Martin. "Art Star" satirizes [[Jet set|jet-set culture]] and features a [[spoken word]] introduction and [[Screaming in music|screaming]] vocals, elements that distinguish it from the band's later releases.{{Cite web |last=Gray |first=Julia |date=June 1, 2018 |title=The 10 best Yeah Yeah Yeahs songs |url=https://stereogum.com/1999279/the-10-best-yeah-yeah-yeahs-songs/lists |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}} "Miles Away" was described as the record's most "ferocious" and "grinding garage" song. {{Short description|2001 EP by Yeah Yeah Yeahs}} {{Use mdy dates|date=June 2025}} {{Infobox album | name = Yeah Yeah Yeahs | type = EP | artist = [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]] | cover = Yeah_Yeah_Yeahs_(EP).jpg | alt = | released = July 9, 2001 | recorded = | venue = | studio = | genre = {{hlist|[[Garage rock]]|[[indie rock]]|[[alternative rock]]}} | length = 13:52 | label = [[Self-released]] | producer = {{hlist|Jerry Teel|Yeah Yeah Yeahs}} | prev_title = | prev_year = | next_title = [[Machine (EP)|Machine]] | next_year = 2002 }} '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made. == Background and recording == In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen Orzolek]]—later becoming known as Karen O—and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard. Although it is self-titled, the EP is sometimes incorrectly referred to as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover. == Music and lyrics == {{Listen | filename = YYYs Bang Sample.ogg | title = "Bang" | description = Sample from "Bang", the EP's opening track }} ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' is a [[garage rock]],{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Betty |date=April 26, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2009/apr/27/yeah-yeahs-pop-review |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}} [[indie rock]], and [[alternative rock]] EP.{{Cite web |date= |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, by Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://yeahyeahyeahs.bandcamp.com/album/yeah-yeah-yeahs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[Bandcamp]] |language=en}} It consists of five tracks and runs for 13 minutes and 52 seconds. The songs were written by Karen O, whose [[staccato]] vocals became a focal point of the record,{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=2002 |title=Another ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. The opening track, "Bang", is about Karen O's sexual dissatisfaction with an ex-boyfriend,{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=August 2002 |title=An ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. Thought you might enjoy reading it. |url=http://www.collapseboard.com/features/interviews/an-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-it/3/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017110318/http://www.collapseboard.com/features/interviews/an-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-it/3/ |archive-date=October 17, 2012 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=Collapse Board}} emphasized by the repeated lyric "As a fuck, son, you sucked!" {{Short description|2001 EP by Yeah Yeah Yeahs}} {{Use mdy dates|date=June 2025}} {{Infobox album | name = Yeah Yeah Yeahs | type = EP | artist = [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]] | cover = Yeah_Yeah_Yeahs_(EP).jpg | alt = | released = July 9, 2001 | recorded = | venue = | studio = | genre = {{hlist|[[Garage rock]]|[[indie rock]]|[[alternative rock]]}} | length = 13:52 | label = [[Self-released]] | producer = {{hlist|Jerry Teel|Yeah Yeah Yeahs}} | prev_title = | prev_year = | next_title = [[Machine (EP)|Machine]] | next_year = 2002 }} '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made. == Background and recording == In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen Orzolek]]—later becoming known as Karen O—and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard. {{Short description|2001 EP by Yeah Yeah Yeahs}} {{Use mdy dates|date=June 2025}} {{Infobox album | name = Yeah Yeah Yeahs | type = EP | artist = [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]] | cover = Yeah_Yeah_Yeahs_(EP).jpg | alt = | released = July 9, 2001 | recorded = | venue = | studio = | genre = {{hlist|[[Garage rock]]|[[indie rock]]|[[alternative rock]]}} | length = 13:52 | label = [[Self-released]] | producer = {{hlist|Jerry Teel|Yeah Yeah Yeahs}} | prev_title = | prev_year = | next_title = [[Machine (EP)|Machine]] | next_year = 2002 }} '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made. == Background and recording == In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen Orzolek]]—later known as Karen O—and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard. Later that year, they changed their name to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted to a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by their observations of the contemporary Ohio music scene.{{Cite web Although it is self-titled, the EP is sometimes incorrectly referred to as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover. == Music and lyrics == {{Listen | filename = YYYs Bang Sample.ogg | title = "Bang" | description = Sample from "Bang", the EP's opening track }} ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' is a [[garage rock]],{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Betty |date=April 26, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2009/apr/27/yeah-yeahs-pop-review |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}} [[indie rock]], and [[alternative rock]] EP.{{Cite web |date= |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, by Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://yeahyeahyeahs.bandcamp.com/album/yeah-yeah-yeahs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[Bandcamp]] |language=en}} It consists of five tracks and runs for 13 minutes and 52 seconds. The opening track, "Bang", is about Karen O's sexual dissatisfaction with an ex-boyfriend,{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=August 2002 |title=An ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made. == Background and recording == In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen Orzolek]]—later known as Karen O—and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early [[punk rock]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a [[garage rock]] record featuring the band's early musical style. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

By late 2001, Yeah Yeah Yeahs gained a following for their live shows.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> Around this time, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce their debut [[Extended play|EP]].<ref name=":1" /> They recorded it at the short-lived Funhouse Recording Studio with Teel, while Chuck Scott [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] it at Soundoptik in New York City. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a record featuring the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

By late 2001, Yeah Yeah Yeahs gained a following for their live shows.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> Around this time, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce their debut [[Extended play|EP]].<ref name=":1" /> They recorded it at the short-lived Funhouse Recording Studio with Teel, while Chuck Scott [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] it at Soundoptik in New York City. Its art and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> Although it is self-titled, the EP is sometimes incorrectly referred to as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a record featuring the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a record featuring the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a record featuring the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made. 

== Background and recording ==

By late 2001, Yeah Yeah Yeahs gained a following for their live shows.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> Around this time, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce their debut [[Extended play|EP]].<ref name=":1" /> They recorded it at the short-lived Funhouse Recording Studio with Teel, while Chuck Scott [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] it at Soundoptik in New York City. Its art and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> Although it is self-titled, the EP is sometimes incorrectly referred to as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />

At [[Metacritic]], which assigns a [[Standard score|normalized]] rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received an [[Weighted arithmetic mean|average]] score of 73, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref name="MC" /> Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were highlighted for additional praise, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795}}</ref><ref name="Blender" /> Some criticism was directed at its [[sound quality]], which was seen as limiting its potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer found three of its five tracks unremarkable.<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />   

In 2002, ''[[NME]]'' ranked ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' second on its list of the year's best singles.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 10, 2016 |title=NME's best albums and tracks of 2002 |url=https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124234412/https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |archive-date=January 24, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |website=[[NME]]}}</ref> In the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', [[Sasha Frere-Jones]] awarded the EP four stars, writing that the band "instantly made their case for good-old-fashioned attitude"; the EP scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' ranked it among the best albums of its year, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2018, ''[[Stereogum]]'' ranked "Art Star" and "Miles Away" among the band's best songs.<ref name=":12" /> In 2024, writers for [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it built on the early works of contemporaries like [[the Strokes]] and [[Interpol (band)|Interpol]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a record featuring the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made. 

== Background and recording ==
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen Orzolek]]—later known as Karen O—and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard. Later that year, they changed their name to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted to a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton By late 2001, Yeah Yeah Yeahs gained a following for their live shows.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> Around this time, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce their debut [[Extended play|EP]].<ref name=":1" /> They recorded it at the short-lived Funhouse Recording Studio with Teel, while Chuck Scott [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] it at Soundoptik in New York City. Its art and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> Although it is self-titled, the EP is sometimes incorrectly referred to as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />

== Music and lyrics ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' is an [[art punk]], [[garage rock]], and [[indie rock]] EP.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Betty |date=April 26, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2009/apr/27/yeah-yeahs-pop-review |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> It consists of five tracks and runs for 13 minutes and 52 seconds.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> The songs were written by Karen O, whose [[staccato]] vocals became a focal point of the record,<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=2002 |title=Another ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. The opening track, "Bang", is about Karen O's sexual dissatisfaction with an ex-boyfriend,<ref>{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=August 2002 |title=An ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. the EP scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' ranked it among the best albums of its year, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2018, ''[[Stereogum]]'' ranked "Art Star" and "Miles Away" among the band's best songs.<ref name=":12" /> In 2024, writers for [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it built on the early works of contemporaries like [[the Strokes]] and [[Interpol (band)|Interpol]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a record featuring the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made. 

== Background and recording ==
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen Orzolek]]—later known as Karen O—and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard. By late 2001, Yeah Yeah Yeahs gained a following for their live shows.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> Around this time, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce their debut [[Extended play|EP]].<ref name=":1" /> They recorded it at the short-lived Funhouse Recording Studio with Teel, while Chuck Scott [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] it at Soundoptik in New York City. Its art and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> Although it is self-titled, the EP is sometimes incorrectly referred to as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />

the EP scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' ranked it among the best albums of its year, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2018, ''[[Stereogum]]'' ranked "Art Star" and "Miles Away" among the band's best songs.<ref name=":12" /> In 2024, writers for [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it built on the early works of contemporaries like [[the Strokes]] and [[Interpol (band)|Interpol]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a record featuring the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

By late 2001, Yeah Yeah Yeahs gained a following for their live shows.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> Around this time, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce their debut [[Extended play|EP]].<ref name=":1" /> They recorded it at the short-lived Funhouse Recording Studio with Teel, while Chuck Scott [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] it at Soundoptik in New York City. the EP scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' ranked it among the best albums of its year, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2018, ''[[Stereogum]]'' ranked "Art Star" and "Miles Away" among the band's best songs.<ref name=":12" /> In 2024, writers for [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it built on the early works of contemporaries like [[the Strokes]] and [[Interpol (band)|Interpol]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a record featuring the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made. 

== Background and recording ==

By late 2001, Yeah Yeah Yeahs gained a following for their live shows.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> Around this time, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce their debut [[Extended play|EP]].<ref name=":1" /> They recorded it at the short-lived Funhouse Recording Studio with Teel, while Chuck Scott [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] it at Soundoptik in New York City. Its art and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> Although it is self-titled, the EP is sometimes incorrectly referred to as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />

the EP scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' ranked it among the best albums of its year, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2018, ''[[Stereogum]]'' ranked "Art Star" and "Miles Away" among the band's best songs.<ref name=":12" /> In 2024, writers for [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it built on the early works of contemporaries like [[the Strokes]] and [[Interpol (band)|Interpol]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a record featuring the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made. 

== Background and recording ==

By late 2001, Yeah Yeah Yeahs gained a following for their live shows.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> Around this time, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce their debut [[Extended play|EP]].<ref name=":1" /> They recorded it at the short-lived Funhouse Recording Studio with Teel, while Chuck Scott [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] it at Soundoptik in New York City. Its art and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> Although it is self-titled, the EP is sometimes incorrectly referred to as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a record featuring the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made.

By late 2001, Yeah Yeah Yeahs gained a following for their live shows.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> Around this time, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce their debut [[Extended play|EP]].<ref name=":1" /> They recorded it at the short-lived Funhouse Recording Studio with Teel, while Chuck Scott [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] it at Soundoptik in New York City. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a record featuring the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made. 

== Background and recording ==
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen Orzolek]]—later known as Karen O—and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard. Later that year, they changed their name to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted to a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton |first=Cillea |date=April 4, 2023 |title=Behind the New York City-inspired band name: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-new-york-city-inspired-band-name-yeah-yeah-yeahs/ Guardian]]}}</ref> In September 2000, they added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup and played their first show as an [[opening act]] for [[the White Stripes]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yashari Fader]]}}</ref>

By late 2001, Yeah Yeah Yeahs gained a following for their live shows.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> Around this time, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce their debut [[Extended play|EP]].<ref name=":1" /> They recorded it at the short-lived Funhouse Recording Studio with Teel, while Chuck Scott [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] it at Soundoptik in New York City. Its art and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> Although it is self-titled, the EP is sometimes incorrectly referred to as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />

== Music and lyrics ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' is an [[art punk]], [[garage rock]], and [[indie rock]] EP.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Betty |date=April 26, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2009/apr/27/yeah-yeahs-pop-review |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> It consists of five tracks and runs for 13 minutes and 52 seconds.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> The songs were written by Karen O, whose [[staccato]] vocals became a focal point of the record,<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=2002 |title=Another ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. This one was their first ever cover story. The opening track, "Bang", is about Karen O's sexual dissatisfaction with an ex-boyfriend,<ref>{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=August 2002 |title=An ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. Thought you might enjoy reading it. |url=http://www.collapseboard.com/features/interviews/an-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-it/3/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017110318/http://www.collapseboard.com/features/interviews/an-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-it/3/ |archive-date=October 17, 2012 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=Collapse Board}}</ref> emphasized by the repeated lyric "As a fuck, son, you sucked!"<ref name=":1" /> Themes of sex and [[masturbation]] are further developed in "Mystery Girl", co-written by the band and Jack Martin.<ref name="RS" /> "Art Star" satirizes [[Jet set|jet-set culture]] and features a [[spoken word]] introduction and [[Screaming in music|screaming]] vocals, elements that distinguish it from the band's later releases.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |last=Gray |first=Julia |date=June 1, 2018 |title=The 10 best Yeah Yeah Yeahs songs |url=https://stereogum.com/1999279/the-10-best-yeah-yeah-yeahs-songs/lists |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref> "Miles Away" is about a woman that has "hurt fewer people in a better world".<ref name=":12" /> The closing track, "Our Time", is an [[anthem]] about perseverance,<ref name=":9" /> which came to inspire New Yorkers after the [[September 11 attacks]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name="RSAG" />

In 2002, ''[[NME]]'' ranked ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' second on its list of the year's best singles.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 10, 2016 |title=NME's best albums and tracks of 2002 |url=https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124234412/https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |archive-date=January 24, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |website=[[NME]]}}</ref> In the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', [[Sasha Frere-Jones]] awarded the EP four stars, writing that the band "instantly made their case for good-old-fashioned attitude"; the EP scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' ranked it among the best albums of its year, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2024, writers for ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'' ranked it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it built on the early works of contemporaries like [[the Strokes]] and [[Interpol (band)|Interpol]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American indie rock band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. After forming in 2000 and building a reputation with their live shows, Yeah Yeah Yeahs recorded and produced the EP with Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]]. It is a record featuring the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in April 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] and [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively.  

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[NME]]'' as the second best single of 2002. It received little attention upon release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] ranked it among the greatest EPs ever made. 

== Background and recording ==
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen Orzolek]]—later known as Karen O—and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard. Later that year, they changed their name to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted to a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton |first=Cillea |date=April 4, 2023 |title=Behind the New York City-inspired band name: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-new-york-city-inspired-band-name-yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250824184119/https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-new-york-city-inspired-band-name-yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=August 24, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[American Songwriter]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hanley |first=Lynsey |date=February 26, 2006 |title=Affirmative action |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2006/feb/26/popandrock.yeahyeahyeahs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231213134047/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2006/feb/26/popandrock.yeahyeahyeahs |archive-date=December 13, 2023 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> In September 2000, they added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup and played their first show as an [[opening act]] for [[the White Stripes]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yashari |first=Leora |date=November 20, 2017 |title=Karen O is (still) pushing boundaries |url=https://www.lennyletter.com/story/karen-o-is-still-pushing-boundaries |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181020230743/https://www.lennyletter.com/story/karen-o-is-still-pushing-boundaries |archive-date=October 20, 2018 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[Lenny Letter]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs Fader]]}}</ref>

By late 2001, Yeah Yeah Yeahs gained a following for their live shows.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> Around this time, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce their debut [[Extended play|EP]].<ref name=":1" /> They recorded it at the short-lived Funhouse Recording Studio with Teel, while Chuck Scott [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] it at Soundoptik in New York City. Its art and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> Although it is self-titled, the EP is sometimes incorrectly referred to as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />

== Music and lyrics ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' is an [[art punk]], [[garage rock]], and [[indie rock]] EP.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Betty |date=April 26, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2009/apr/27/yeah-yeahs-pop-review |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> It consists of five tracks and runs for 13 minutes and 52 seconds.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> The songs were written by Karen O, whose [[staccato]] vocals became a focal point of the record,<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=2002 |title=Another ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. This one was their first ever cover story. Thought you might enjoy reading this as well. |url=https://collapseboard.com/another-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-this-one-was-their-first-ever-cover-story-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-this-as-well/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191121173149/https://collapseboard.com/another-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-this-one-was-their-first-ever-cover-story-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-this-as-well/ |archive-date=November 21, 2019 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=Collapse Board}}</ref> and its music was composed by the band.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rogers |first=Jude |author-link=Jude Rogers |date=March 14, 2019 |title='I just wanted to write a love song that stands the test of time': Karen O on her best work |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2019/mar/14/all-i-ever-wanted-to-do-was-write-a-love-song-that-stands-the-test-of-time-karen-o-on-her-best-songs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The rock band [[ESG (band)|ESG]] served as a primary influence, with the band attempting to recreate their sound "with guitar instead of bass."<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2014 |title=Karen O: soundtrack of my life |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831054959/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |archive-date=August 31, 2014 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> Other influences include the rock bands [[Blondie (band)|Blondie]], [[The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion|Jon Spencer Blues Explosion]], and [[Tommy James and the Shondells]].<ref name=":11" />{{Listen

The opening track, "Bang", is about Karen O's sexual dissatisfaction with an ex-boyfriend,<ref>{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=August 2002 |title=An ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. Thought you might enjoy reading it. |url=http://www.collapseboard.com/features/interviews/an-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-it/3/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017110318/http://www.collapseboard.com/features/interviews/an-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-it/3/ |archive-date=October 17, 2012 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=Collapse Board}}</ref> emphasized by the repeated lyric "As a fuck, son, you sucked!"<ref name=":1" /> Themes of sex and [[masturbation]] are further developed in "Mystery Girl", co-written by the band and Jack Martin.<ref name="RS" /> "Art Star" satirizes [[Jet set|jet-set culture]] and features a [[spoken word]] introduction and [[Screaming in music|screaming]] vocals, elements that distinguish it from the band's later releases.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |last=Gray |first=Julia |date=June 1, 2018 |title=The 10 best Yeah Yeah Yeahs songs |url=https://stereogum.com/1999279/the-10-best-yeah-yeah-yeahs-songs/lists |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref> "Miles Away" is about a woman that has "hurt fewer people in a better world".<ref name=":12" /> The closing track, "Our Time", is an [[anthem]] about perseverance,<ref name=":9" /> which came to inspire New Yorkers after the [[September 11 attacks]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name="RSAG" />
