'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. It received little attention upon it's frst release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it as among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. It received little attention upon it's frst release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it as among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. It received little attention upon it's frst release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it as among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted to a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. It received little attention upon it's frst release but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted to a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton == Release ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was [[self-released]] by the band on July 9, 2001, through their own Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. It initially received little attention but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted to a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. It initially received little attention but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted to a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton |first=Cillea |date=April 4, 2023 |title=Behind the New York City-inspired band name: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-new-york-city-inspired-band-name-yeah-yeah-yeahs/ Guardian]]}}</ref> In September 2000, they added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. It initially received little attention but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted to a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton |first=Cillea |date=April 4, 2023 |title=Behind the New York City-inspired band name: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-new-york-city-inspired-band-name-yeah-yeah-yeahs/ Guardian]]}}</ref> In September 2000, they added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' consists of five tracks.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> Karen O wrote all of the lyrics, while the music was co-written by the band.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |last=Rogers |first=Jude |author-link=Jude Rogers |date=March 14, 2019 |title='I just wanted to write a love song that stands the test of time': Karen O on her best work |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2019/mar/14/all-i-ever-wanted-to-do-was-write-a-love-song-that-stands-the-test-of-time-karen-o-on-her-best-songs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The [[dance-punk]] and [[funk]] band [[ESG (band)|ESG]] served as a primary influence for the music, while the band attempting to recreate ESG's sound "with guitar instead of bass."<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2014 |title=Karen O: soundtrack of my life |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831054959/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |archive-date=August 31, 2014 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> They also aimed to capture the "cocky attitude" they had whilst performing live.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's [[staccato]] vocals became a focal point of the record, though she described her singing as "really, really, really sloshed."<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=2002 |title=Another ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. It initially received little attention but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted to a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton |first=Cillea |date=April 4, 2023 |title=Behind the New York City-inspired band name: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-new-york-city-inspired-band-name-yeah-yeah-yeahs/ Guardian]]}}</ref> In September 2000, they added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live == Music and lyrics ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' consists of five tracks.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> Karen O wrote all of the lyrics, while the music was co-written by the band.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |last=Rogers |first=Jude |author-link=Jude Rogers |date=March 14, 2019 |title='I just wanted to write a love song that stands the test of time': Karen O on her best work |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2019/mar/14/all-i-ever-wanted-to-do-was-write-a-love-song-that-stands-the-test-of-time-karen-o-on-her-best-songs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The [[dance-punk]] and [[funk]] band [[ESG (band)|ESG]] served as a primary influence for the music, while the band attempting to recreate ESG's sound "with guitar instead of bass."<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2014 |title=Karen O: soundtrack of my life |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831054959/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |archive-date=August 31, 2014 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> They also aimed to capture the "cocky attitude" they had whilst performing live.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's [[staccato]] vocals became a focal point of the record, though she described her singing as "really, really, really sloshed."<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=2002 |title=Another ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. This one was their first ever cover story. Thought you might enjoy reading this as well. |url=https://collapseboard.com/another-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-this-one-was-their-first-ever-cover-story-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-this-as-well/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191121173149/https://collapseboard.com/another-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-this-one-was-their-first-ever-cover-story-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-this-as-well/ |archive-date=November 21, 2019 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=Collapse Board}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berman |first=Stuart |date=August 16, 2003 |title=A conversation with Karen O, Nick Zinner, and Brian Chase of the Yeah Yeah Yeahs |magazine=[[Eye Weekly]] |page=23 |pages=}}</ref> Other influences include the rock bands [[Blondie (band)|Blondie]], [[The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion|Jon Spencer Blues Explosion]], and [[Tommy James and the Shondells]].<ref name=":11" />{{Listen

The opening track, "Bang", is about Karen O's sexual dissatisfaction with an ex-boyfriend,<ref>{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=August 2002 |title=An ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. It initially received little attention but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] founded the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted to a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton |first=Cillea |date=April 4, 2023 |title=Behind the New York City-inspired band name: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-new-york-city-inspired-band-name-yeah-yeah-yeahs/ Guardian]]}}</ref> In September 2000, they added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live == Music and lyrics ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' consists of five tracks.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> Karen O wrote all of the lyrics, while the music was co-written by the band.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |last=Rogers |first=Jude |author-link=Jude Rogers |date=March 14, 2019 |title='I just wanted to write a love song that stands the test of time': Karen O on her best work |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2019/mar/14/all-i-ever-wanted-to-do-was-write-a-love-song-that-stands-the-test-of-time-karen-o-on-her-best-songs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The [[dance-punk]] and [[funk]] band [[ESG (band)|ESG]] served as a primary influence for the music, while the band attempting to recreate ESG's sound "with guitar instead of bass."<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2014 |title=Karen O: soundtrack of my life |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831054959/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |archive-date=August 31, 2014 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> They also aimed to capture the "cocky attitude" they had whilst performing live.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's [[staccato]] vocals became a focal point of the record, though she described her singing as "really, really, really sloshed."<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=2002 |title=Another ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. It initially received little attention but became a [[sleeper hit]] after its reissue, topping the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and exceeding sales of 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The Yeah Yeah Yeahs' singer [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted towards a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton |first=Cillea |date=April 4, 2023 |title=Behind the New York City-inspired band name: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-new-york-city-inspired-band-name-yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250824184119/https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-new-york-city-inspired-band-name-yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=August 24, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[American Songwriter]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hanley |first=Lynsey |date=February 26, 2006 |title=Affirmative action |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2006/feb/26/popandrock.yeahyeahyeahs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231213134047/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2006/feb/26/popandrock.yeahyeahyeahs |archive-date=December 13, 2023 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> In September 2000, they added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a live following.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio, which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":0" /> The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />

== Music and lyrics ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' consists of five tracks.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> Karen O wrote all of the lyrics, while the music was co-written by the band.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |last=Rogers |first=Jude |author-link=Jude Rogers |date=March 14, 2019 |title='I just wanted to write a love song that stands the test of time': Karen O on her best work |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2019/mar/14/all-i-ever-wanted-to-do-was-write-a-love-song-that-stands-the-test-of-time-karen-o-on-her-best-songs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The [[dance-punk]] and [[funk]] band [[ESG (band)|ESG]] served as a primary influence for the music, while the band attempting to recreate ESG's sound "with guitar instead of bass."<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2014 |title=Karen O: soundtrack of my life |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831054959/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |archive-date=August 31, 2014 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> They also aimed to capture the "cocky attitude" they had whilst performing live.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's [[staccato]] vocals became a focal point of the record, though she described her singing as "really, really, really sloshed."<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=2002 |title=Another ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. This one was their first ever cover story. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. The EP received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The Yeah Yeah Yeahs' singer [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted towards a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio, which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":0" /> The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />

== Music and lyrics ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' consists of five tracks.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> Karen O wrote all of the lyrics, while the music was co-written by the band.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |last=Rogers |first=Jude |author-link=Jude Rogers |date=March 14, 2019 |title='I just wanted to write a love song that stands the test of time': Karen O on her best work |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2019/mar/14/all-i-ever-wanted-to-do-was-write-a-love-song-that-stands-the-test-of-time-karen-o-on-her-best-songs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The [[dance-punk]] and [[funk]] band [[ESG (band)|ESG]] served as a primary influence for the music, while the band attempting to recreate ESG's sound "with guitar instead of bass."<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2014 |title=Karen O: soundtrack of my life |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831054959/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |archive-date=August 31, 2014 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> They also aimed to capture the "cocky attitude" they had whilst performing live.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's [[staccato]] vocals became a focal point of the record, though she described her singing as "really, really, really sloshed."<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=2002 |title=Another ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. This one was their first ever cover story. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. The EP received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. The EP received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Music and lyrics ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' consists of five tracks.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> Karen O wrote all of the lyrics, while the music was co-written by the band.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |last=Rogers |first=Jude |author-link=Jude Rogers |date=March 14, 2019 |title='I just wanted to write a love song that stands the test of time': Karen O on her best work |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2019/mar/14/all-i-ever-wanted-to-do-was-write-a-love-song-that-stands-the-test-of-time-karen-o-on-her-best-songs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The [[dance-punk]] and [[funk]] band [[ESG (band)|ESG]] served as a primary influence for the music, while the band attempting to recreate ESG's sound "with guitar instead of bass."<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2014 |title=Karen O: soundtrack of my life |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831054959/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |archive-date=August 31, 2014 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> They also aimed to capture the "cocky attitude" they had whilst performing live.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's [[staccato]] vocals became a focal point of the record, though she described her singing as "really, really, really sloshed."<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=2002 |title=Another ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. This one was their first ever cover story. Thought you might enjoy reading this as well. |url=https://collapseboard.com/another-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-this-one-was-their-first-ever-cover-story-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-this-as-well/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191121173149/https://collapseboard.com/another-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-this-one-was-their-first-ever-cover-story-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-this-as-well/ |archive-date=November 21, 2019 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=Collapse Board}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berman |first=Stuart |date=August 16, 2003 |title=A conversation with Karen O, Nick Zinner, and Brian Chase of the Yeah Yeah Yeahs |magazine=[[Eye Weekly]] |page=23 |pages=}}</ref> Other influences include the rock bands [[Blondie (band)|Blondie]], [[The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion|Jon Spencer Blues Explosion]], and [[Tommy James and the Shondells]].<ref name=":11" />{{Listen

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. The EP received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The Yeah Yeah Yeahs' singer [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. |first=Cillea |date=April 4, 2023 |title=Behind the New York City-inspired band name: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-new-york-city-inspired-band-name-yeah-yeah-yeahs/ == Music and lyrics ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' consists of five tracks.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> Karen O wrote all of the lyrics, while the music was co-written by the band.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |last=Rogers |first=Jude |author-link=Jude Rogers |date=March 14, 2019 |title='I just wanted to write a love song that stands the test of time': Karen O on her best work |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2019/mar/14/all-i-ever-wanted-to-do-was-write-a-love-song-that-stands-the-test-of-time-karen-o-on-her-best-songs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The [[dance-punk]] and [[funk]] band [[ESG (band)|ESG]] served as a primary influence for the music, while the band attempting to recreate ESG's sound "with guitar instead of bass."<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2014 |title=Karen O: soundtrack of my life |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831054959/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |archive-date=August 31, 2014 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> They also aimed to capture the "cocky attitude" they had whilst performing live.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's [[staccato]] vocals became a focal point of the record, though she described her singing as "really, really, really sloshed."<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=2002 |title=Another ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. This one was their first ever cover story. Thought you might enjoy reading this as well. |url=https://collapseboard.com/another-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-this-one-was-their-first-ever-cover-story-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-this-as-well/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191121173149/https://collapseboard.com/another-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-this-one-was-their-first-ever-cover-story-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-this-as-well/ |archive-date=November 21, 2019 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=Collapse Board}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berman |first=Stuart |date=August 16, 2003 |title=A conversation with Karen O, Nick Zinner, and Brian Chase of the Yeah Yeah Yeahs |magazine=[[Eye Weekly]] |page=23 |pages=}}</ref> Other influences include the rock bands [[Blondie (band)|Blondie]], [[The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion|Jon Spencer Blues Explosion]], and [[Tommy James and the Shondells]].<ref name=":11" />{{Listen

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. The EP received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The Yeah Yeah Yeahs' singer [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and shifted towards a "trashy, punky, [and] grimy" sound inspired by the contemporary Ohio music scene.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Houghton |first=Cillea |date=April 4, 2023 |title=Behind the New York City-inspired band name: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-new-york-city-inspired-band-name-yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250824184119/https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-new-york-city-inspired-band-name-yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=August 24, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[American Songwriter]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hanley |first=Lynsey |date=February 26, 2006 |title=Affirmative action |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2006/feb/26/popandrock.yeahyeahyeahs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231213134047/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2006/feb/26/popandrock.yeahyeahyeahs |archive-date=December 13, 2023 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> In September 2000, they added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a live following.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio, which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":0" /> The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />

== Music and lyrics ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' consists of five tracks.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> Karen O wrote all of the lyrics, while the music was co-written by the band.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |last=Rogers |first=Jude |author-link=Jude Rogers |date=March 14, 2019 |title='I just wanted to write a love song that stands the test of time': Karen O on her best work |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2019/mar/14/all-i-ever-wanted-to-do-was-write-a-love-song-that-stands-the-test-of-time-karen-o-on-her-best-songs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The [[dance-punk]] and [[funk]] band [[ESG (band)|ESG]] served as a primary influence for the music, while the band attempting to recreate ESG's sound "with guitar instead of bass."<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2014 |title=Karen O: soundtrack of my life |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831054959/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/aug/29/karen-o-soundtrack-of-my-life-yeah-yeah-yeahs |archive-date=August 31, 2014 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> They also aimed to capture the "cocky attitude" they had whilst performing live.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's [[staccato]] vocals became a focal point of the record, though she described her singing as "really, really, really sloshed."<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=2002 |title=Another ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. This one was their first ever cover story. Thought you might enjoy reading this as well. |url=https://collapseboard.com/another-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-this-one-was-their-first-ever-cover-story-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-this-as-well/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191121173149/https://collapseboard.com/another-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-this-one-was-their-first-ever-cover-story-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-this-as-well/ |archive-date=November 21, 2019 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=Collapse Board}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berman |first=Stuart |date=August 16, 2003 |title=A conversation with Karen O, Nick Zinner, and Brian Chase of the Yeah Yeah Yeahs |magazine=[[Eye Weekly]] |page=23 |pages=}}</ref> Other influences include the rock bands [[Blondie (band)|Blondie]], [[The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion|Jon Spencer Blues Explosion]], and [[Tommy James and the Shondells]].<ref name=":11" />{{Listen
| filename     = YYYs Bang Sample.ogg
| title        = "Bang"
| description  = Sample from "Bang", the EP's opening track
}}

The opening track, "Bang", is about Karen O's sexual dissatisfaction with an ex-boyfriend,<ref>{{Cite web |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=August 2002 |title=An ancient interview with Yeah Yeah Yeahs. Thought you might enjoy reading it. |url=http://www.collapseboard.com/features/interviews/an-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-it/3/ |url-status=live |archive-date=October 17, 2012 |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=Collapse Board}}</ref> emphasized by the repeated lyric "As a fuck, son, you sucked!"<ref name=":1" /> The band co-wrote "Mystery Girl" with Jack Martin, which is about a sexually-promiscuous woman and her adventures.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="Pitchfork" /> The lyrics of "[[Art Star]]" satirizes [[Jet set|jet-set culture]] and the art world, and it is the only Yeah Yeah Yeahs song with a [[spoken word]] introduction and [[Screaming in music|screaming]] vocals.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |last=Gray |first=Julia |date=June 1, web |last=Frere-Jones |first=Sasha |author-link=Sasha Frere-Jones |date=February 6, 2006 |title=Positive attitude |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2006/02/13/positive-attitude |url-status=live == Release ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was [[self-released]] by the band on July 9, 2001, through their own Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. After gaining significant media coverage for a high-profile performance at [[South by Southwest]] in 2002,{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}} it was reissued by [[Independent record label|independent labels]] such as [[Touch and Go Records]] in the United States and [[Wichita Recordings]] in the United Kingdom.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 At [[Metacritic]], which assigns a [[Standard score|normalized]] rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received an [[Weighted arithmetic mean|average]] score of 73, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref name="MC" /> Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were espically praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795}}</ref><ref name="Blender" /> Some critics noted its [[Lo-fi music|low-fi]] sound quality, which was seen as limiting the music's potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer described the song-writing of three of its five tracks "unremarkable".<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />

In 2002, ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' ranked ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' among the best singles of the year, with ''NME'' placing it second.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pareles |first=Jon |author-link=Jon Pareles |date=December 29, 2002 |title=Music: The year in review, the critics/the 10 best albums; somber anthems, loose-limbed funk |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/12/29/arts/music-year-review-critics-10-best-albums-somber-anthems-loose-limbed-funk-536792.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210210202523/https://www.nytimes.com/2002/12/29/arts/music-year-review-critics-10-best-albums-somber-anthems-loose-limbed-funk-536792.html |archive-date=February 10, 2021 |access-date=April 10, 2026 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 10, 2016 |title=NME's best albums and tracks of 2002 |url=https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124234412/https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |archive-date=January 24, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |website=[[NME]]}}</ref>{{Efn|Although released in 2001, the EP was not recognized by either publication until its 2002 reissue.}} That year, it placed as number 40 in ''[[The Village Voice]]''<nowiki/>'s [[Pazz & Jop]] poll.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Christgau |first=Robert |author-link=Robert Christgau |date=2002 |title=The 2002 Pazz & Jop critics poll |url=https://www.robertchristgau.com/xg/pnj/pjres02.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260212065438/https://www.robertchristgau.com/xg/pnj/pjres02.php |archive-date=February 12, 2026 |access-date=April 10, 2026 |website=robertchristgau.com}}</ref> In the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', [[Sasha Frere-Jones]] awarded the EP four stars, writing that the band "instantly made their case for good-old-fashioned attitude"; the EP scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' called it one of 2001's best albums, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2024, ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'' ranked it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it bested the early works by two of their contemporaries, [[the Strokes]] and [[Interpol (band)|Interpol]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was received positively by critics and ranked by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' among the best releases of 2002. The EP received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 units in the United States by the end of the decade. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==
The Yeah Yeah Yeahs' singer [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the acoustic duo Unitard in 2000. At [[Metacritic]], which assigns a [[Standard score|normalized]] rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received an [[Weighted arithmetic mean|average]] score of 73, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref name="MC" /> Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were espically praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795}}</ref><ref name="Blender" /> Some critics noted its [[Lo-fi music|low-fi]] sound quality, which was seen as limiting the music's potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer described the song-writing of three of its five tracks "unremarkable".<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />

In 2002, ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' ranked ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' among the best singles of the year, with ''NME'' placing it second.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pareles |first=Jon |author-link=Jon Pareles |date=December 29, 2002 |title=Music: The year in review, the critics/the 10 best albums; '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 units by the end of the decade. The EP was received positively by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the greatest EPs ever made.

== Background and recording ==

At [[Metacritic]], which assigns a [[Standard score|normalized]] rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received an [[Weighted arithmetic mean|average]] score of 73, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref name="MC" /> Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were espically praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795}}</ref><ref name="Blender" /> Some critics noted its [[Lo-fi music|low-fi]] sound quality, which was seen as limiting the music's potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer described the song-writing of three of its five tracks "unremarkable".<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />

In 2002, ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' ranked ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' among the best singles of the year, with ''NME'' placing it second.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pareles |first=Jon |author-link=Jon Pareles |date=December 29, 2002 |title=Music: The year in review, the critics/the 10 best albums; '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 units by the end of the decade. The EP was received positively by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

At [[Metacritic]], which assigns a [[Standard score|normalized]] rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received an [[Weighted arithmetic mean|average]] score of 73, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref name="MC" /> Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were espically praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795}}</ref><ref name="Blender" /> Some critics noted its [[Lo-fi music|low-fi]] sound quality, which was seen as limiting the music's potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer described the song-writing of three of its five tracks "unremarkable".<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />

In 2002, ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' ranked ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' among the best singles of the year, with ''NME'' placing it second.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pareles |first=Jon |author-link=Jon Pareles |date=December 29, 2002 |title=Music: The year in review, the critics/the 10 best albums; somber anthems, loose-limbed funk |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/12/29/arts/music-year-review-critics-10-best-albums-somber-anthems-loose-limbed-funk-536792.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210210202523/https://www.nytimes.com/2002/12/29/arts/music-year-review-critics-10-best-albums-somber-anthems-loose-limbed-funk-536792.html |archive-date=February 10, 2021 |access-date=April 10, 2026 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 10, 2016 |title=NME's best albums and tracks of 2002 |url=https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124234412/https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |archive-date=January 24, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |website=[[NME]]}}</ref>{{Efn|Although released in 2001, the EP was not recognized by either publication until its 2002 reissue.}} That year, it placed as number 40 in ''[[The Village Voice]]''<nowiki/>'s [[Pazz & Jop]] poll.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Christgau |first=Robert |author-link=Robert Christgau |date=2002 |title=The 2002 Pazz & Jop critics poll |url=https://www.robertchristgau.com/xg/pnj/pjres02.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260212065438/https://www.robertchristgau.com/xg/pnj/pjres02.php |archive-date=February 12, 2026 |access-date=April 10, 2026 |website=robertchristgau.com}}</ref> In the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', [[Sasha Frere-Jones]] awarded the EP four stars, writing that the band "instantly made their case for good-old-fashioned attitude"; '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 units by the end of the decade. The EP was received positively by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

At [[Metacritic]], which assigns a [[Standard score|normalized]] rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received an [[Weighted arithmetic mean|average]] score of 73, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref name="MC" /> Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were espically praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795}}</ref><ref name="Blender" /> Some critics noted its [[Lo-fi music|low-fi]] sound quality, which was seen as limiting the music's potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer described the song-writing of three of its five tracks "unremarkable".<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />

In 2002, ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' ranked ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' among the best singles of the year, with ''NME'' placing it second.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pareles |first=Jon |author-link=Jon Pareles |date=December 29, 2002 |title=Music: The year in review, the critics/the 10 best albums; somber anthems, loose-limbed funk |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/12/29/arts/music-year-review-critics-10-best-albums-somber-anthems-loose-limbed-funk-536792.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210210202523/https://www.nytimes.com/2002/12/29/arts/music-year-review-critics-10-best-albums-somber-anthems-loose-limbed-funk-536792.html |archive-date=February 10, 2021 |access-date=April 10, 2026 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 10, 2016 |title=NME's best albums and tracks of 2002 |url=https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124234412/https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |archive-date=January 24, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |website=[[NME]]}}</ref>{{Efn|Although released in 2001, the EP was not recognized by either publication until its 2002 reissue.}} That year, it placed as number 40 in ''[[The Village Voice]]''<nowiki/>'s [[Pazz & Jop]] poll.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Christgau |first=Robert |author-link=Robert Christgau |date=2002 |title=The 2002 Pazz & Jop critics poll |url=https://www.robertchristgau.com/xg/pnj/pjres02.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260212065438/https://www.robertchristgau.com/xg/pnj/pjres02.php |archive-date=February 12, 2026 |access-date=April 10, 2026 |website=robertchristgau.com}}</ref> In the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', [[Sasha Frere-Jones]] awarded the EP four stars, writing that the band "instantly made their case for good-old-fashioned attitude"; the EP scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' called it one of 2001's best albums, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2024, ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'' ranked it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it bested the early works by two of their contemporaries, [[the Strokes]] and [[Interpol (band)|Interpol]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 units by the end of the decade. The EP was received positively by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":0" /> The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />

== Release ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was [[self-released]] by the band on July 9, 2001, through their own Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. At [[Metacritic]], which assigns a [[Standard score|normalized]] rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received an [[Weighted arithmetic mean|average]] score of 73, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref name="MC" /> Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were espically praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795}}</ref><ref name="Blender" /> Some critics noted its [[Lo-fi music|low-fi]] sound quality, which was seen as limiting the music's potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer described the song-writing of three of its five tracks "unremarkable".<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />

In 2002, ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' ranked ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' among the best singles of the year, with ''NME'' placing it second.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pareles |first=Jon |author-link=Jon Pareles |date=December 29, 2002 |title=Music: The year in review, the critics/the 10 best albums; somber anthems, loose-limbed funk |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/12/29/arts/music-year-review-critics-10-best-albums-somber-anthems-loose-limbed-funk-536792.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210210202523/https://www.nytimes.com/2002/12/29/arts/music-year-review-critics-10-best-albums-somber-anthems-loose-limbed-funk-536792.html |archive-date=February 10, 2021 |access-date=April 10, 2026 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 10, 2016 |title=NME's best albums and tracks of 2002 |url=https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124234412/https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |archive-date=January 24, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |website=[[NME]]}}</ref>{{Efn|Although released in 2001, the EP was not recognized by either publication until its 2002 reissue.}} That year, it placed as number 40 in ''[[The Village Voice]]''<nowiki/>'s [[Pazz & Jop]] poll.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Christgau |first=Robert |author-link=Robert Christgau |date=2002 |title=The 2002 Pazz & Jop critics poll |url=https://www.robertchristgau.com/xg/pnj/pjres02.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260212065438/https://www.robertchristgau.com/xg/pnj/pjres02.php |archive-date=February 12, 2026 |access-date=April 10, 2026 |website=robertchristgau.com}}</ref> In the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', [[Sasha Frere-Jones]] awarded the EP four stars, writing that the band "instantly made their case for good-old-fashioned attitude"; the EP scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' called it one of 2001's best albums, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2024, ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'' ranked it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it bested the early works by two of their contemporaries, [[the Strokes]] and [[Interpol (band)|Interpol]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' (often mistitled as '''''Master''''') is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States, [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom, and other [[Independent record label|independent labels]] worldwide. The EP was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, a member of [[Boss Hog]], and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 units by the end of the decade. The EP was received positively by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="timesonline20092">{{cite web |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=June 13, 2009 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs: why fans of the art-punk trio can't say no |url=http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615161512/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/music/article6485717.ece |archive-date=June 15, 2011 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":0" /> The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover.<ref name=":1" />
