'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States in 2002. The EP, which was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received positively by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":0" /> The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

The opening track, "Bang", was inspired by Karen O's sexual dissatisfaction with an ex-boyfriend, emphasized by the repeated lyric "As a fuck, son, you sucked!"<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=True |first=Everett |author-link=Everett True |date=August 2002 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs FAQ |url=http://www.collapseboard.com/features/interviews/an-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-it/3/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017110318/http://www.collapseboard.com/features/interviews/an-ancient-interview-with-yeah-yeah-yeahs-thought-you-might-enjoy-reading-it/3/ |archive-date=October 17, 2012 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |magazine=BB Gun |via=''Collapse Board''}}</ref> The band co-composed "Mystery Girl" with Jack Martin, a session guitarist,<ref name="SGOurTime" /> which is about a sexually-promiscuous woman and her adventures.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="Pitchfork" />

The lyrics of "[[Art Star]]" satirizes [[Jet set|jet-set culture]] and the art world, and it is the only Yeah Yeah Yeahs song with a [[spoken word]] introduction and [[Screaming in music|screaming]] vocals.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |last=Gray |first=Julia |date=June 1, 2018 |title=The 10 best Yeah Yeah Yeahs songs |url=https://stereogum.com/1999279/the-10-best-yeah-yeah-yeahs-songs/lists |access-date=March 7, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260111202417/https://stereogum.com/1999279/the-10-best-yeah-yeah-yeahs-songs/lists|archive-date=January 11, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=Frere-Jones |first=Sasha |author-link=Sasha Frere-Jones |date=February 6, 2006 |title=Positive attitude |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2006/02/13/positive-attitude |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230401151503/https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2006/02/13/positive-attitude |archive-date=April 1, 2023 |access-date=March 26, 2026 |website=[[The New Yorker]]}}</ref> "Miles Away" is about a woman that has "hurt fewer people in a better world".<ref name=":12" />

"Our Time", the closing track and first song written by the band,{{Efn|Originally titled "Time to Be Hated".<ref name=":13" /><ref name="SGOurTime">{{Cite web |last=DeVille |first=Chris |date=September 24, 2020 |title=Watch Yeah Yeah Yeahs play "Our Time" at their first show, 20 years ago today |url=https://stereogum.com/2099961/yeah-yeah-yeahs-first-show-mercury-lounge/news |access-date=March 28, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815220314/https://www.stereogum.com/2099961/yeah-yeah-yeahs-first-show-mercury-lounge/news/|archive-date=August 15, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>}}<ref name=":13" /> is an anthem about perseverance and a romance that nearly failed, which came to inspire New Yorkers after the [[September 11 attacks]].<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":8" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name="RSAG" />

== Release ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was [[self-released]] by the band on July 9, 2001, through their own Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure in late 2001 after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> Label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

At [[Metacritic]], which assigns a [[Standard score|normalized]] rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received an [[Weighted arithmetic mean|average]] score of 73, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref name="MC" /> Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were especially praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795|access-date=April 15, 2026|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825201420/https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2#v=onepage&q&f=false|archive-date=August 25, 2022|publisher=[[CMJ]]}}</ref><ref name="Blender" />

Some critics noted its [[Lo-fi music|low-fi]] quality, which was seen as limiting its commercial potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer described three of its five tracks as "unremarkable".<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the UK and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the US. The EP, which was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received positively by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":0" /> The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

|author-link=Jude Rogers |date=March 14, 2019 |title='I just wanted to write a love song that stands the test of time': Karen O on her best work |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2019/mar/14/all-i-ever-wanted-to-do-was-write-a-love-song-that-stands-the-test-of-time-karen-o-on-her-best-songs |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The == Release ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was [[self-released]] by the band on July 9, 2001, through their own Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure in late 2001 after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> Label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

At [[Metacritic]], which assigns a [[Standard score|normalized]] rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received an [[Weighted arithmetic mean|average]] score of 73, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref name="MC" /> Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were especially praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795|access-date=April 15, 2026|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825201420/https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2#v=onepage&q&f=false|archive-date=August 25, 2022|publisher=[[CMJ]]}}</ref><ref name="Blender" />

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the UK and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the US. The EP, which was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received positively by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":0" /> The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was [[self-released]] by the band on July 9, 2001, through their own Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure in late 2001 after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> Label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

At [[Metacritic]], which assigns a [[Standard score|normalized]] rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received an [[Weighted arithmetic mean|average]] score of 73, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref name="MC" /> Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were especially praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795|access-date=April 15, 2026|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825201420/https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2#v=onepage&q&f=false|archive-date=August 25, 2022|publisher=[[CMJ]]}}</ref><ref name="Blender" /> Some critics noted its [[Lo-fi music|low-fi]] quality, which was seen as limiting its commercial potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer described three of its five tracks as "unremarkable".<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />

In 2002, both ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]'' ranked ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' among the best singles of the year, with ''NME'' placing it second,{{Efn|Although released in 2001, the EP was not recognized by either publication until its 2002 reissue.}}<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pareles |first=Jon |author-link=Jon Pareles |date=December 29, 2002 |title=Music: The year in review, the critics/the 10 best albums; somber anthems, loose-limbed funk |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/12/29/arts/music-year-review-critics-10-best-albums-somber-anthems-loose-limbed-funk-536792.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210210202523/https://www.nytimes.com/2002/12/29/arts/music-year-review-critics-10-best-albums-somber-anthems-loose-limbed-funk-536792.html |archive-date=February 10, 2021 |access-date=April 10, 2026 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 10, 2016 |title=NME's best albums and tracks of 2002 |url=https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124234412/https://www.nme.com/features/2002-2-1045353 |archive-date=January 24, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |website=[[NME]]}}</ref> while ''[[The Village Voice]]'' ranked it at number 40 on their [[Pazz & Jop]] poll.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Christgau |first=Robert |author-link=Robert Christgau |date=2002 |title=The 2002 Pazz & Jop critics poll |url=https://www.robertchristgau.com/xg/pnj/pjres02.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260212065438/https://www.robertchristgau.com/xg/pnj/pjres02.php |archive-date=February 12, 2026 |access-date=April 10, 2026 |website=robertchristgau.com}}</ref> In the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', [[Sasha Frere-Jones]] awarded the EP four stars, writing that the band "instantly made their case for good-old-fashioned attitude"; the EP scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' called it one of 2001's best albums, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2024, ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'' ranked it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it bested the early works of some contemporaries.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the UK and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the US. The EP, which was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":0" /> The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was [[self-released]] by the band on July 9, 2001, through their own Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure in late 2001 after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> Label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the UK and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the US. The EP, which was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.}<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was [[self-released]] by the band on July 9, 2001, through their own Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure in late 2001 after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> Label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the UK and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the US. The EP, which was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was [[self-released]] by the band on July 9, 2001, through their own Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure in late 2001 after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> Label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the UK and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the US. The EP, which was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was [[self-released]] by the band on July 9, 2001, through their own Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure in late 2001 after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> Label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the UK and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the US. The EP, which was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was [[self-released]] by the band on July 9, 2001, through their own Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure in late 2001 after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> Label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the UK and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the US. The EP, which was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' was [[self-released]] by the band on July 9, 2001, through their own Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure in late 2001 after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> Label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the UK and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the US. The EP, which was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention and sold poorly until its 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by the [[independent record label|independent]] record labels [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the UK and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the US. The EP was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' received little attention until the 2002 reissue, after which it topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}
