'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. The EP was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001 and sold poorly until reissued in 2002 by the [[independent record label|independent]] record labels [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the UK and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the US.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences. The EP was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001 and sold poorly until reissued in 2002 by the [[independent record label|independent]] record labels [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the UK and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the US.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were especially praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795|access-date=April 15, 2026|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825201420/https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2#v=onepage&q&f=false|archive-date=August 25, 2022|publisher=[[CMJ]]}}</ref><ref name="Blender" /> Some critics noted its [[Lo-fi music|low-fi]] quality, which was seen as limiting its commercial potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer described three of its five tracks as "unremarkable".<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desire to share their music.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desires to share their music and secure more shows.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=We just wanted to play at clubs and entertain ourselves. And honestly, we didn't have anything better to do. We were bored. New York City was boring for us at the time. [...] Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration.}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab On Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desires to share their music and secure more shows.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=We just wanted to play at clubs and entertain ourselves. And honestly, we didn't have anything better to do. We were bored. New York City was boring for us at the time. [...] Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration.}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.<ref name=":0" />{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab on Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref> offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2010 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bright Eyes help Wichita celebrate 10th anniversary |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126052644/https://pitchfork.com/news/38347-yeah-yeah-yeahs-bright-eyes-help-wichita-celebrate-10th-anniversary/ |archive-date=January 26, 2025 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Pitchfork (magazine)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was received favorably by critics and ranked among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desires to share their music and secure more shows.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=We just wanted to play at clubs and entertain ourselves. And honestly, we didn't have anything better to do. We were bored. New York City was boring for us at the time. [...] Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration.}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin while performing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> The label executive Mark Bowen was impressed after he heard "Bang" online, offering the band a deal with [[Wichita Recordings]] to redistribute the EP in the United Kingdom in April 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab on Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. '''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded as a [[Demo (music)|demo]] over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and originally not intended for release. However, the band felt a desire to share their music in hopes of landing more shows. Musically, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences, while lead singer and songwriter [[Karen O]] explores themes of romance, sex, and humor in her lyrics.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was received favorably by critics for its sound and Karen O's performances, and was named among the best releases of 2002 by publications like ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desires to share their music and secure more shows.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=We just wanted to play at clubs and entertain ourselves. And honestly, we didn't have anything better to do. We were bored. New York City was boring for us at the time. [...] Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration.}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>
