'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded as a [[Demo (music)|demo]] over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and was not intended for release. However, the band wanted to share their music in hopes of landing more shows. Musically, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences, while lead singer and songwriter [[Karen O]] explores themes of romance, sex, and humor in her lyrics.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was praised by critics for its unique sound and Karen O's performances, and named among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desires to share their music and secure more shows.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=We just wanted to play at clubs and entertain ourselves. And honestly, we didn't have anything better to do. We were bored. New York City was boring for us at the time. [...] Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration.}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin during a performance on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" />

The [[Wichita Recordings]] co-founder Mark Bowen was impressed after hearing "Bang", and in April 2002 offered to redistribute the EP in the U.K.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab on Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded as a [[Demo (music)|demo]] over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and was not intended for release. However, the band wanted to share their music in hopes of landing more shows. Musically, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences, while lead singer and songwriter [[Karen O]] explores themes of romance, sex, and humor in her lyrics.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was praised by critics for its unique sound and Karen O's performances, and named among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desires to share their music and secure more shows.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=We just wanted to play at clubs and entertain ourselves. And honestly, we didn't have anything better to do. We were bored. New York City was boring for us at the time. [...] Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration.}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin during a performance on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" />

The [[Wichita Recordings]] co-founder Mark Bowen was impressed after hearing "Bang", and in April 2002 offered to redistribute the EP in the U.K.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab on Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded as a [[Demo (music)|demo]] over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and was not intended for release. However, the band wanted to share their music in hopes of landing more shows. Musically, ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences, while lead singer and songwriter [[Karen O]] explores themes of romance, sex, and humor in her lyrics.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. The EP was praised by critics for its unique sound and Karen O's performances, and named among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desires to share their music and secure more shows.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=We just wanted to play at clubs and entertain ourselves. And honestly, we didn't have anything better to do. We were bored. New York City was boring for us at the time. [...] Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration.}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin during a performance on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" />

The [[Wichita Recordings]] co-founder Mark Bowen was impressed after hearing "Bang", and in April 2002 offered to redistribute the EP in the U.K.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab on Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded as a [[Demo (music)|demo]] over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and was not intended for release. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences, and lead singer and lyricist [[Karen O]]'s themes of romance, sex and humor.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was praised by critics for its unique sound and Karen O's performances, and named among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desires to share their music and secure more shows.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=We just wanted to play at clubs and entertain ourselves. And honestly, we didn't have anything better to do. We were bored. New York City was boring for us at the time. [...] Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration.}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin during a performance on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" />

The [[Wichita Recordings]] co-founder Mark Bowen was impressed after hearing "Bang", and in April 2002 offered to redistribute the EP in the U.K.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab on Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded as a [[Demo (music)|demo]] over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and was not intended for release. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences, and lead singer and lyricist [[Karen O]]'s themes of romance, sex and humor.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was praised by critics for its unique sound and Karen O's performances, and named among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desires to share their music and secure more shows.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=We just wanted to play at clubs and entertain ourselves. And honestly, we didn't have anything better to do. We were bored. New York City was boring for us at the time. [...] Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration.}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin during a performance on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" />

The [[Wichita Recordings]] co-founder Mark Bowen was impressed after hearing "Bang", and in April 2002 offered to redistribute the EP in the U.K.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab on Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded as a [[Demo (music)|demo]] over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and was not intended for release. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences, and lead singer and lyricist [[Karen O]]'s themes of romance, sex and humor.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was praised by critics for its unique sound and Karen O's performances, and named among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desires to share their music and secure more shows.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=We just wanted to play at clubs and entertain ourselves. And honestly, we didn't have anything better to do. We were bored. New York City was boring for us at the time. [...] Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration.}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin during a performance on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" />

The [[Wichita Recordings]] co-founder Mark Bowen was impressed after hearing "Bang", and in April 2002 offered to redistribute the EP in the U.K.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab on Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while the English journalist [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were especially praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795|access-date=April 15, 2026|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825201420/https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2#v=onepage&q&f=false|archive-date=August 25, 2022|publisher=[[CMJ]]}}</ref><ref name="Blender" /> Some critics noted that its [[Lo-fi music|low-fi]] sytle and production limited its commercial potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer described three of its five tracks as "unremarkable".<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />

In the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', the critic [[Sasha Frere-Jones]] awarded the EP four stars, writing that the band "instantly made their case for good-old-fashioned attitude"; the EP eventually scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' named it as one of 2001's best albums, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2024, ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'' placed it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it bested the early works of some contemporaries.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded as a [[Demo (music)|demo]] over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and was not intended for release. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences, and lead singer and lyricist [[Karen O]]'s themes of romance, sex and humor.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was praised by critics for its unique sound and Karen O's performances, and named among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]]. However, they ultimately developed the demo into their debut EP, a decision that Zinner attributes to their desires to share their music and secure more shows.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}}<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=We just wanted to play at clubs and entertain ourselves. And honestly, we didn't have anything better to do. We were bored. New York City was boring for us at the time. [...] Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration.}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin during a performance on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" />

The [[Wichita Recordings]] co-founder Mark Bowen was impressed after hearing "Bang", and in April 2002 offered to redistribute the EP in the U.K.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=After hearing this song we got in touch with them, but were amazed they had no record deal. We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to Arab on Radar; Karen O was already a superstar in every way. Months later Jo Whiley played the record at lunchtime on Radio 1 (despite its liberal use of the word "fuck" in the chorus) and everyone went nuts. It was our first top 40 hit.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] in July 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while the English journalist [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were especially praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795|access-date=April 15, 2026|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825201420/https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2#v=onepage&q&f=false|archive-date=August 25, 2022|publisher=[[CMJ]]}}</ref><ref name="Blender" /> Some critics noted that its [[Lo-fi music|low-fi]] sytle and production limited its commercial potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer described three of its five tracks as "unremarkable".<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />

In the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', the critic [[Sasha Frere-Jones]] awarded the EP four stars, writing that the band "instantly made their case for good-old-fashioned attitude"; the EP eventually scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' named it as one of 2001's best albums, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2024, ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'' placed it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it bested the early works of some contemporaries.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded as a [[Demo (music)|demo]] over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and developed into their debut EP to land more shows. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences, and lead singer and lyricist [[Karen O]]'s themes of romance, sex and humor.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was praised by critics for its unique sound and Karen O's performances, and named among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]] that was developed into their debut EP.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} Zinner explained in an interview that "Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration."<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin during a performance on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> 

[[Wichita Recordings]] co-founder Mark Bowen was impressed after hearing "Bang", and was surprised to see that the band had yet to sign with a record label. According to Bowen, "We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to [[Arab on Radar]]; Karen O was already a superstar in every way."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=}}</ref> He offered them distribution of the EP in the United Kingdom in 2002.<ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States in July 2002, after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] earlier that year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

Critics generally praised the EP's sound; [[AllMusic]] described it as one of the most innovative releases of the 2000s [[Garage rock|garage rock revival]] at the time,<ref name="AllMusic" /> while the English journalist [[Everett True]] wrote that it captured the spirit of rock n' roll.<ref name=":9" /> Karen O's performances were especially praised, with writers for [[Blender (magazine)|''Blender'']] and ''[[CMJ]]'' describing her vocals as "hot and sexy".<ref name=":11">{{cite magazine |last=Santangelo |first=Antonia |date=July 8, 2002 |title=Reviews |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2 |magazine=CMJ New Music Report |page=12 |volume=72 |issue=770 |issn=0890-0795|access-date=April 15, 2026|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825201420/https://books.google.com/books?id=aBw3t2fY64UC&pg=PA10-IA2#v=onepage&q&f=false|archive-date=August 25, 2022|publisher=[[CMJ]]}}</ref><ref name="Blender" /> Some critics noted that its [[Lo-fi music|low-fi]] sytle and production limited its commercial potential,<ref name="RS" /> while a [[Stylus Magazine|''Stylus'']] writer described three of its five tracks as "unremarkable".<ref name="Stylus" /> [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']] noted early skepticism surrounding the rock movement but concluded that the EP demonstrated a "sharp survey" of the band's capabilities.<ref name="Pitchfork" />

In the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', the critic [[Sasha Frere-Jones]] awarded the EP four stars, writing that the band "instantly made their case for good-old-fashioned attitude"; the EP eventually scored higher than their acclaimed debut album, ''[[Fever to Tell]]''.<ref name="RSAG" /> In 2016, ''[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]'' named it as one of 2001's best albums, and said that it was essential both to the band's success and the contemporary [[Music of New York City|New York music scene]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Berlyant |first=Matthew |date=December 29, 2016 |title=The 15th anniversary: Yeah Yeah Yeahs' "Yeah Yeah Yeahs" EP |url=https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221192539/https://www.undertheradarmag.com/news/the_15th_anniversary_yeah_yeah_yeahs_yeah_yeah_yeahs_ep/ |archive-date=February 21, 2024 |access-date=March 24, 2026 |magazine=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]]}}</ref> In 2024, ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'' placed it at number 42 on their list of the "100 Greatest EPs of All Time", writing that it bested the early works of some contemporaries.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The 100 Greatest EPs of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130195229/https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/greatest-albums/the-100-greatest-eps-of-all-time |archive-date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=March 6, 2026 |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]}}</ref>

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded as a [[Demo (music)|demo]] over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and developed into their debut EP to land more shows. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences, and lead singer and lyricist [[Karen O]]'s themes of romance, sex and humor.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was praised by critics for its unique sound and Karen O's performances, and named among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]] that was developed into their debut EP.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} Zinner explained in an interview that "Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration."<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin during a performance on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> 

[[Wichita Recordings]] co-founder Mark Bowen was impressed after hearing "Bang", and was surprised to see that the band had yet to sign with a record label. According to Bowen, "We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to [[Arab on Radar]]; Karen O was already a superstar in every way."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=}}</ref> He offered them distribution of the EP in the United Kingdom in 2002.<ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States in July 2002, after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] earlier that year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded as a [[Demo (music)|demo]] over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and developed into their debut EP to land more shows. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences, and lead singer and lyricist [[Karen O]]'s themes of romance, sex and humor.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was praised by critics for its unique sound and Karen O's performances, and named among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
[[File:Yyy2003.png|alt=A woman and two men photographed mid-concert in 2003|left|thumb|Yeah Yeah Yeahs performing in 2003. From left to right: [[Karen O]], [[Brian Chase]] and [[Nick Zinner]].]]
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]] that was developed into their debut EP.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} Zinner explained in an interview that "Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration."<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>

== Release ==
The band [[self-released]] ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' on July 9, 2001, through their Shifty label,<ref name=":0" /> and received little attention on release. However, the band and the EP gained some exposure later that year after [[Albert Hammond Jr.]] of [[the Strokes]] wore their pin during a performance on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref name=":14" /> 

[[Wichita Recordings]] co-founder Mark Bowen was impressed after hearing "Bang", and was surprised to see that the band had yet to sign with a record label. According to Bowen, "We flew to America and saw them play fourth on the bill to [[Arab on Radar]]; Karen O was already a superstar in every way."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Mark |date=July 9, 2010 |title=Ten years of Wichita Recordings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809164454/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2010/jul/08/ten-years-wichita-recordings |archive-date=August 9, 2025 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |website=[[The Guardian]] |quote=}}</ref> He then offered them distribution of the EP in the United Kingdom in 2002.<ref>{{Cite AV media notes |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |year=2002 |publisher=[[Wichita Recordings]] |id=WEBB029T |type=Vinyl liner notes |others=[[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]}}</ref> [[Touch and Go Records]] reissued it in the United States in July 2002, after seeing a high-profile concert at [[South by Southwest]] earlier that year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260208165424/http://www.touchandgorecords.com/bands/album.php?id=107 |archive-date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026 |website=touchandgorecords.com |publisher=[[Touch and Go Records]]}}</ref>{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=236}}{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=245}}

'''''Yeah Yeah Yeahs''''' is the debut [[extended play]] (EP) by the American [[indie rock]] band [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs]]. It was [[self-released]] on July 9, 2001, and reissued in 2002 by [[Wichita Recordings|Wichita]] in the United Kingdom and [[Touch and Go Records|Touch and Go]] in the United States. It was recorded as a [[Demo (music)|demo]] over two days in early 2001 with producer Jerry Teel, and developed into their debut EP to land more shows. ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' features the band's early [[garage rock]] and [[art punk]] influences, and lead singer and lyricist [[Karen O]]'s themes of romance, sex and humor.

''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' topped the [[UK Independent Singles and Albums Charts|UK Indie Chart]] and had sold over 71,000 copies by the end of the decade. It was praised by critics for its unique sound and Karen O's performances, and named among the best releases of 2002 by ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[NME]]''. In 2024, [[Paste (magazine)|''Paste'']] placed it among the 100 greatest EPs of all time.

== Background and recording ==
In 2000, singer/songwriter [[Karen O]] and guitarist [[Nick Zinner]] formed the duo Unitard. They changed their name that year to Yeah Yeah Yeahs and added drummer [[Brian Chase]] to the lineup, forming a trio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brazeal |first=Anne |date=September 8, 2014 |title=Original buzz: Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215050728/https://www.thefader.com/2014/09/08/yeah-yeah-yeahs-interview-2003 |archive-date=December 15, 2025 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[The Fader]]}}</ref> By early 2001, the band earned a following for their live performances.<ref name="RS" /> During this period, they enlisted Jerry Teel, a former guitarist for the punk rock band [[Boss Hog]], to co-produce a [[Demo (music)|demo]] that was developed into their debut EP.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} Zinner explained in an interview that "Our first EP was recorded as a demo, so we could get shows at cool clubs opening up for bigger bands. That was literally our aspiration."<ref name=":15">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs on love songs, New York and transforming on stage |url=https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102854/https://www.npr.org/2013/04/14/176830368/yeah-yeah-yeahs-on-love-songs-new-york-and-transforming-on-stage |archive-date=August 15, 2025 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |quote=}}</ref> 

The ''Yeah Yeah Yeahs'' EP was recorded across two days with Teel at [[Avenue B (Manhattan)|Avenue B]]'s Funhouse Recording Studio,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2006 |title=Yeah Yeah Yeahs |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420074329/https://www.clashmusic.com/features/yeah-yeah-yeahs/ |archive-date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=April 12, 2026 |website=[[Clash (magazine)|Clash]]}}</ref> which doubled as their rehearsal space. It was [[Mastering (audio)|mastered]] by Chuck Scott at Soundoptik in New York City.{{Sfn|Goodman|2017|p=229}} The artwork and packaging were designed by the band and Crispin.<ref name=":0" /> The front cover contains a [[close-up]] of a topless Karen O, while the back cover features three different [[Selfie|self-photographs]] of her, Zinner and Chase.<ref name=":0" /> Although the EP is self-titled, it is sometimes mistitled as ''Master'' due to the necklace Karen O wears on the cover, or as ''Bang'' after its opening track.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=July 9, 2021 |title=The Yeah Yeah Yeahs EP turns 20 |url=https://stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606053222/https://www.stereogum.com/2153436/yeah-yeah-yeahs-debut-ep/reviews/the-anniversary/ |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref>
